newsitem.title: USA: GKN to buy Sinter for $570 million.
newsitem.headline: GKN to buy Sinter for $570 million.

text.p: British engineering giant GKN Plc said Wednesday it will acquire Sinter Metals Inc., an auto parts supplier that is a leading maker of precision-tooled metal components, for $570 million in cash.
GKN's offer works out to about $37 per Sinter share, compared with Tuesday's closing price of $27. Sinter jumped $9.625 to close at $36.625 on the New York Stock Exchange Wednesday.
The price includes $386 million for Sinter's equity and $184 million for the assumption of debt.
Cleveland-based Sinter has operations in the United States, Canada, Germany and Sweden. The company posted pretax profits of $24 million in 1996 based on sales of $373 million.
In addition to supplying the auto industry, Sinter makes parts for home appliances, power tools and the garden industry. GKN said Sinter's management would remain in the merged company.

GKN said it expected the acquisition to boost earnings within a year after closing. The deal, which has the backing of 43 percent of Sinter's outstanding shares including a large stake held by Sinter Chairman Joseph Carreras, is expected to close in late May.
GKN, which makes car components, helicopters and armoured vehicles, also faces a continuing U.S. court battle over the misuse of advertising fees in lawsuits brought by U.S. affiliates.

In one of the biggest awards ever by a U.S. court against a British company, GKN was ordered last month to pay $601 million in damages to U.S. franchises of Meineke Discount Mufflers after a jury found it had misused advertising fees.
GKN has said it plans to appeal the ruling.

News of the Sinter acquisition put an end to speculation that GKN would seek to acquire Vickers Group Plc, maker of Rolls-Royce cars. Shares of Vickers had risen sharply in London in recent days in anticipation of a takeover bid, but fell after the Sinter deal was reported.
Traders said the deal would face little opposition from Sinter shareholders.
"It obviously is a friendly deal," said one New York-based takeover trader.
GKN's stock also rallied, climbing 39-1/2 pence (64 cents) to 951 pence ($15.41) on the London Stock Exchange.
